text:
alisha: Kicking off key-remap sweep across clouds for cust-batch-9. Orchestrator started. Seeing bursts of 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED on GCP and intermittent 429s from Azure KV. Need someone to own adaptive throttling and a quick RBAC checklist before we proceed further.

jon: I can take throttling. Proposal: per-key and per-tenant rate limiting + global in-flight cap. Use full jitter backoff and a small circuit-breaker that quiesces a troubled key for a window.

jon: Backoff sketch:
```
base_ms = 150
max_ms = 60000
wait = min(max_ms, base_ms * 2**attempt)
sleep = rand(0, wait)
```
Also: token-bucket per-tenant (burst=8, rate=4/s) and health-state for key endpoints to avoid tight retry loops.

kevin: Cloud differences matter: AWS has ReEncrypt which is server-side for S3-managed envelopes; prefer that when available. GCP KMS requires decrypt+encrypt for envelope keys (more IO). Azure Key Vault supports unwrap/wrap of data keys; if customers use Managed HSM, wrapKey ops are rate-limited differently. I'll validate Vault SKU and note any soft-delete/rotation behaviors.

mike: Audit requirements: every rewrap must emit a single-line CSV row and a structured log entry with old_key_id,new_key_id,object_uri,method,principal,timestamp,run_id. SOC must be able to query mappings without key access. We'll gate KMS permissions and expose only metadata via a secure view.

alisha: RBAC checklist draft for infra repo: minimal perms only. GCP snippet: 
```
- role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
  members:
  - serviceAccount:rewrap-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- role: roles/cloudkms.viewer
  members:
  - serviceAccount:rewrap-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
AWS: inline policy with kms:ReEncrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:DescribeKey limited to ARN list of keys. Azure: Key Vault data plane permissions wrapKey, unwrapKey, get, list for the service principal.

jon: Error handling plan: mark per-object status in rewrap_table with state (pending, in-progress, success, failed) and error_code. Retry with backoff up to MAX_RETRIES (default 4). If still failing, move to dead-letter queue with context (attempts, last_error, partial_steps). Never delete old ciphertext until new object passes integrity check.

kevin: Important: do not rely on key aliases changing mid-run. If a key owner rotates alias or rotates KMS version under the same alias, it can break idempotency. We should snapshot key version IDs at start and reference versions rather than aliases for the run.

mike: Compliance asks for retention: logs + mapping CSV retained for 7 years, artifacts stored in secure bucket with lifecycle and org-level encryption. SOC will get a read-only "rewrap-audit" role that has logging.viewer + view access to mapping objects but no KMS permissions.

alisha: SRE: can you temporarily raise KMS quotas for project redwood-prod in us-central1 while we run? We'll cap orchestrator throughput and revert when complete.

sre: Temporarily increased GCP KMS quota for redwood-prod in us-central1 until 04:00 UTC. Watching error rate and will roll back if no issues. Alerting on >0.5% KMS error rate over 10m.

kevin: I'll run a 2k-object perf run comparing AWS ReEncrypt vs GCP Decrypt+Encrypt vs Azure wrapKey and post p50/p95/p99 and estimated egress costs. Also include script so we can reproduce.

jon: Metrics to add: rewrap.objects_started, rewrap.objects_succeeded, rewrap.objects_failed, rewrap.kms_rate_limited, rewrap.key_circuit_open. Dashboard with heatmap by tenant and key_id.

mike: Security note: do not log plaintext data keys or plaintext objects. Log only key identifiers, ciphertext metadata, and hashes. Use a KMS-bound signing key for run manifest signatures.

alisha: Runbook updates: added sections "snapshot-key-versions", "safe-commit-step", "dead-letter triage", and a sample KQL/CloudTrail filter for auditors. Artifacts: mapping CSV (old_key_id,new_key_id,object_count,timestamp,run_id) uploaded to gs://redwood-secure/rewrap/<run_id>.csv with ACL=private.

deploy-bot: rewrap-orchestrator v2 rolled to prod at 1840012355 :rocket:

alisha: Quick recap:
- Jon: implement token-bucket, backoff+jitter, circuit-breaker, metrics + dashboard
- Kevin: perf run across clouds + script
- Mike: audit CSV schema, retention policy, SOC read-only role
- SRE: keep temporary quota bump; monitor and report
- Alisha: finalize runbook, ensure mapping CSV artifact and manifest are uploaded

mike: One more: add automated verification step that compares old->new ciphertext SHA256 and object size before marking success; flag any divergence for manual review.

alisha: Agreed. If anything new shows up I'll re-open this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
